edges.description: Expressed in cultured endothelial cells and melanocytes, the mutant made the cells independent of growth factors by upregulating MAPK signalling; the steps from there to the tumour's lymphatic-type endothelium are not established. A later series found no GNA14 mutation in five further KHEs, and the 2020 review leaves open whether such mutations cause the tumour.

The nodules infiltrate across tissue planes, into the dermis, fat, muscle and bone. In mouse haemangioendothelioma cells, overexpression of PROX1 induced an invasive phenotype in vivo, a model of a link between the lymphatic programme and infiltration rather than a study of human tumours.
In most patients the infiltrating tumour presents as a soft-tissue mass with skin findings.
Pain can come from the infiltrating, destructive growth.
The infiltrating tumour invades the joints near it.
The tumour invades and destroys bone.

Lymphoedema can follow the tumour, more often when it is large (10 cm or more), mixed and in a limb. On lymphoscintigraphy of 25 patients, 24 of them with a limb tumour, lymphatic stasis within the involved lesion was found in all 22 with abnormal findings, and lymphoedema was on the side of the lesion, as it was in all 13 affected patients of the cohort of 118. The 2020 review suggests that a tumour of the proximal limb, particularly at or near the inguinal or axillary lymph nodes, may influence lymphatic development or damage the lymphatic vessels, and reports a hypothesis that, for such tumours, obstruction of lymphatic flow during the acute Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon may lead to lymphoedema; it adds that inflammation may also play a role. In the cohort of 118, of whom 13 had lymphoedema, a history of the phenomenon and sirolimus treatment were not significant predictors of lymphoedema; with 13 cases this does not exclude them. The lymphoscintigraphy series' abstract names no centre, so whether it shares patients with the cohort of 118 is not known.
The tumour vasculature traps platelets. Infiltration into muscle or deeper, and a retroperitoneal or intrathoracic site, are associated with a higher likelihood of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.
Trapping and consumption of platelets lowers the platelet count.

Anaemia accompanies the falling platelet count of the phenomenon. The cited sources name the anaemia of the phenomenon as microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, and intralesional haemorrhage among its consequences, without tracing the steps from trapping to anaemia.

nodes.description: The tumour grows as infiltrating nodules of spindled endothelial cells lining slit-like or crescentic vessels. The endothelium stains for CD31 and CD34 and for the lymphatic markers LYVE1, PROX1 and podoplanin (D2-40), and not for GLUT-1. Angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis are dysregulated and progressive. How fast the endothelium proliferates is not settled: the cohort of 70 reports Ki-67 on the endothelial cells, while in the lesion the 2020 review illustrates only a few nuclei stained for it. The 2020 review adds VEGFR-3 to these lymphatic markers; in a thoracic series of 7 KHEs and 6 kaposiform lymphangiomatoses, all lesions examined had spindle tumour cells staining for CD31 and D2-40, and CD31-positive cells isolated from three of six patients' tumours carried CD31, Ki-67 and LYVE1 in culture. Which signals drive the programme is not established. The review suggests, from the expression of both in KHE, that the VEGF-C/VEGFR3 axis may contribute to the tumour's aggressive behaviour, while serum VEGF-C was lower in KHE patients with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, a different compartment from the tissue, against a comparison group the abstract does not state. Serum angiopoietin-2 was 14-fold raised in KHE when the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon was present and not when it was absent, and the serum study proposes it, with the angiopoietin-1 that was lower alongside VEGF-C, as a marker of the phenomenon's coagulopathy. The review offers vascular remodelling, such as vessel sprouting and inflammatory lymphangiogenesis, as a possible explanation of the rise, raises the possibility of a paracrine effect on the tumour's endothelial cells, and also raises the possibility of a role for angiopoietin-2 in the phenomenon itself.

nodes.description: The cause of most tumours is unknown. A somatic activating GNA14 variant (c.614A>T, p.Gln205Leu) was found in one KHE in the 2016 discovery study, a finding the 2020 review gives as 1/3 of KHE specimens; a later sequencing series of five KHEs and two tufted angiomas found none. The mutations reported in KHE are sporadic, not germline. GNA14 belongs to the GNAQ family, whose G alpha subunits bind G-protein-coupled receptors. No cited source establishes the cell in which the variant arises within the tumour, so no cell is bound here. The node covers only tumours carrying the variant (one KHE in the cited studies), and even there the review leaves open whether it is a cause or a later change in the tumour.
